The *Kuṇḍalakesātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 21) is a verse narrative preserved in the Therīapadāna section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the background and past deeds of the senior nun Kuṇḍalakesā. SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages and notes a thematic or cross-referential connection with the *Sulasājātaka* (Ja 419) [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates significant internal alignment with other Pali works, recording 500 matching passages across 67 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its longest sustained correspondence is with the commentary to the *Therīgāthā* (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, segments §10.2–52.1), along with shared material in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §31.1–35.4) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also extensively shares standard formulaic segments (notably §14.1–22.3) with adjacent hagiographies of prominent nuns in the Therīapadāna, including the *Khemātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 18), *Uppalavaṇṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 19), *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 22), and *Dhammadinnātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 23) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Northern Buddhist works, most prominently the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (best score 70) and *Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇīsūtra*, as well as several Tibetan canonical sutras including the *Samādhirājasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
